card: Splits the CreateNewBlock_validity unit test into independent test cases and eliminates mutable state shared across test sections. Miner subtests previously shared an in-memory blockchain and required manual Tip()->nHeight decrements between runs, while basic mining tests reused and mutated a single transaction instance across checks. The PR has each test case mine its own fixture chain using hardcoded nonces and builds test transactions declaratively. It affects only unit test code.
changed_since_previous: No functional or structural changes to the PR scope; diff is now available.
evidence: Commit 7e81f5046e notes that subtests 'ran as member functions on one shared chain, so each started from the state the previous one left behind and the caller had to patch Tip()->nHeight between them.'
Commit 838e901e90 and diff show replacing sequential field mutations on a single mutable transaction with in-place declarative construction for each test case.
problem: Subtests in CreateNewBlock_validity ran sequentially on a shared blockchain, creating implicit inter-test state dependencies and requiring manual chain tip height adjustments (decrementing Tip()->nHeight) between calls. Similarly, TestBasicMining repeatedly mutated fields of a single CMutableTransaction across test sections, obscuring transaction preconditions and making tests difficult to debug or isolate.

risk.why: A mistake would only cause unit test failures or test coverage gaps in block template construction.

summary: Splits the monolithic CreateNewBlock_validity miner unit test into separate, independent BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE instances (package_selection, sigops_adjusted_weight_chunk_limit, basic_mining, prioritised_mining). Each case now sets up its own 110-block fixture chain using a shared MineBlockInfoChain helper. In addition, transactions within basic_mining are constructed declaratively rather than by mutating a single shared transaction object across sections.
